results.finding: The intro reader predicted all nine sections in order, the evidence kinds (worked fictional example, quoted Stripe limits, Stripe's 2025 post, Orb's documentation, dated acquisition) and the tone.

results.draft_locus: Introduction ¶4
results.quote: the two acquisitions of 2026 with the status of token billing, and the comparison of the two providers
results.finding: The intro reader could name only one acquisition (Adyen/Orb), did not know what token billing is, and predicted 'a comparison of Stripe and Orb' where the section compares Stripe and Adyen. The introduction never names Metronome or says which two providers are compared.

Cold reader: duplicates need an identifier assigned where the event is created (provider-generated ids make each resend new), owned by the producer, plus the receiver's memory window; late batch: acceptance window, billing cut-off (three days exceeds even 72 h), correction path (later-invoice line or credit note), explicitly 'accepted but never billed'. Matches expected.

Cold reader: yes at invoice time (€30 billed later), no with real-time drawdown; two consistency models with different costs; documented examples basic meters (invoice time) vs Metronome (real time). Matches expected.

Orb's design is consistently attributed ('Orb's statement about Orb ... not a description of Adyen's platform'; comparison table 'Not public for Adyen; Orb's documentation about Orb'); Adyen's own sentence on Orb is quoted as Adyen's. Metronome is described only by documented integration and features and explicitly placed on neither side of the design choice.
